messages.subject: [statnet_help] A question about ERGMs and simulating networks with an arbitrary number of nodes
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] A question about ERGMs and simulating networks with an arbitrary number of nodes
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statnet List,

I have been playing with statnet a bit for a hobby project, and am a  
bit confused about drawing sample networks using "simulate" and a  
model fitted using the ergm function.

This may be a result of my poor understanding of the theory of ERGMs  
in general, but I was wondering if it is possible to simulate a  
network with more or less nodes than the original network -- i.e.  
simulate a network that is larger/smaller than the original but with  
similar statistical characteristics in the ERGM sense.

For example, let's say I fit an ERGM model using the full  
faux.magnolia graph (1400 nodes or so, but only wish to generate  
sample networks with, say, 20 actors but with the same ERGM model  
characteristics. Is there any way to do this? And does the question  
even make sense....? :-)

Any advice would be much appreciated.

kind regards,

-- Hannu Rajaniemi

messages.subject: [statnet_help] A question about ERGMs and simulating networks with an arbitrary number of nodes
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] A question about ERGMs and simulating networks with an arbitrary number of nodes
messages.body_plain:
Hi Hannu.  In general, the question comes down to what you mean by  
"similar statistical characteristics".  It turns out that this phrase  
is not always so easy to define in terms of the only thing that  
matters about a network in the context of a specific ERGM, namely, the  
vector of network statistics.  Thus, your question is best answered  
with another question:  What do you mean precisely by "the same ERGM  
model characteristics"?

(I should add that this question is sometimes fairly easy to answer  
satisfactorily, sometimes not!)

Dave

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Off topic: upcoming postdoctoral positions in Cambridge, England
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statnet List,

I apologize that this is off-topic, but I'm looking for a couple of 
highly technical postdoctoral students to work on social and sexual 
networks. One position (up to 2 years) involves the use of bipartite 
ERGMs to model people and the places they socialize and meet sexual 
partners, with some modeling of dynamic bipartite networks. The second 
(up to 4 years) involves modeling respondent-driven sampling 
(www.respondentdrivensampling.org). Both positions require a healthy 
knowledge of C/C++, R (or Python), a keen interest in statistical models 
(especially ERGMs, causal inference), networks, and simulation. The 
positions will be the Department of Veterinary Medicine at the 
University of Cambridge, which also houses the Cambridge Infectious 
Disease Consortium (http://www.vet.cam.ac.uk/cidc/). The positions 
aren't 100% official yet, as I am trying to transfer funds from the US 
to the UK - no mean feat! Please feel free to email me for further 
information.

Best
Simon

messages.subject: [statnet_help] plot.network() with colored edges
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm worried that I'm just being dumb here, but I seem to be stuck.  I'm 
trying to draw a network in which edges are colored according to some 
vertex attribute.  Specifically, I have a sexual contact network with 
sero-status measured for the vertices. I want all edges connecting to a 
positive vertex to be colored, say, red. I seem to be missing something 
about the sort order for the edge list.  I think this simple code 
reproduces the problem I'm having with real data.  I create a network 
object from a simulated edge list.  I then arbitrarily infect nodes 17, 
22, and 44. I create a dummy vector (which I also attach as an edge 
attribute) indicating whether or not an edge is incident with an 
infected vertex.  When I plot the network, the coloring does not come 
out the way I expected it to.

set.seed(1234567)
n1 <- round(1+50*runif(100))
n2 <- round(1+50*runif(100))
eee <- cbind(n1,n2)[order(n1),]
net <- network(eee,directed=FALSE)

edge.status <- rep(0,100)
aaa <- eee[,1]==17 | eee[,2]==17
edge.status[aaa] <- 1
aaa <- eee[,1]==22 | eee[,2]==22
edge.status[aaa] <- 1
aaa <- eee[,1]==44 | eee[,2]==44
edge.status[aaa] <- 1

net %e% "edge.status" <- edge.status
status <- rep(0,51)
status[c(17,22,44)] <- 1

plot(net,
      vertex.col=1+status,
      vertex.cex=1,
      edge.lwd=2,
      edge.col=1+edge.status)

I hope someone can help illuminate what I'm doing wrong here.

A somewhat related question: is there a way to extract an edge list as 
one sees when summarizing a network, summary(net)?

Sorry if I'm just being obtuse -- it is getting late...

Cheers,

Jamie

--

messages.subject: [statnet_help] plot.network() with colored edges
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Jamie -

James Holland Jones wrote:
> Hi all,
> 
> I'm worried that I'm just being dumb here, but I seem to be stuck.  I'm 
> trying to draw a network in which edges are colored according to some 
> vertex attribute.  Specifically, I have a sexual contact network with 
> sero-status measured for the vertices. I want all edges connecting to a 
> positive vertex to be colored, say, red. I seem to be missing something 
> about the sort order for the edge list.  I think this simple code 
> reproduces the problem I'm having with real data.  I create a network 
> object from a simulated edge list.  I then arbitrarily infect nodes 17, 
> 22, and 44. I create a dummy vector (which I also attach as an edge 
> attribute) indicating whether or not an edge is incident with an 
> infected vertex.  When I plot the network, the coloring does not come 
> out the way I expected it to.
> 
<snip>
> 
> I hope someone can help illuminate what I'm doing wrong here.

The %e% operator is a front-end to set.edge.value, which expects edges 
to be listed in their adjacency matrix order.  To adjust edge attributes 
in edge ID order, you need to use set.edge.attribute.  In your case,

set.edge.attribute(net,"edge.status",edge.status+1)
plot(net,vertex.col=1+status,edge.col="edge.status")

seems to produce the desired result.  (Note that edge.col uses matrix 
order, too, but can also take attributes as arguments.)

> 
> A somewhat related question: is there a way to extract an edge list as 
> one sees when summarizing a network, summary(net)?

Yes:

as.matrix(net,matrix.type="edgelist")

Hope that helps,

-Carter

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Problem with transitive term?
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

This is my first message to the list. I have been using R for network research and have some experience with sna and igraph but I just started working with ergm and come across this peculiar situation. The term "transitive" gives some wildly erratic counts for transitive triad counts when entered as an argument in a summary function. Here are some examples (compare it with the triadcensus of the corresponding triad types--which I believe give the correct count):

## Example 1 (bernoulli graph with 5 nodes)

> g.sim <- simulate(network(5) ~ transitive);
Warning message:
In simulate.formula(network(5) ~ transitive) :
  No parameter values given, using Bernouli network
> summary(g.sim ~ transitive);
transitive 
         7 
> summary(g.sim ~ triadcensus(c(8,11,12,15)));
triadcensus.030T triadcensus.120D triadcensus.120U  triadcensus.300 
               2                0                4                1 

## Example 2 (bernoulli graph with 10 nodes)

> g.sim <- simulate(network(10) ~ transitive);
Warning message:
In simulate.formula(network(10) ~ transitive) :
  No parameter values given, using Bernouli network
> summary(g.sim ~ transitive);
transitive 
        18 
> summary(g.sim ~ triadcensus(c(8,11,12,15)));
triadcensus.030T triadcensus.120D triadcensus.120U  triadcensus.300 
               7               10                7                2 

## Example 3 (bernoulli graph with 100 nodes)

> g.sim <- simulate(network(100) ~ transitive);
Warning message:
In simulate.formula(network(100) ~ transitive) :
  No parameter values given, using Bernouli network
> summary(g.sim ~ transitive);
transitive 
    158966 
> summary(g.sim ~ triadcensus(c(8,11,12,15)));
triadcensus.030T triadcensus.120D triadcensus.120U  triadcensus.300 
             118                1                4                0 

## Example 4 (bernoulli graph with 1000 nodes)

> g.sim <- simulate(network(1000) ~ transitive);
Warning message:
In simulate.formula(network(1000) ~ transitive) :
  No parameter values given, using Bernouli network
> summary(g.sim ~ transitive);
transitive 
 166164655 
> summary(g.sim ~ triadcensus(c(8,11,12,15)));
triadcensus.030T triadcensus.120D triadcensus.120U  triadcensus.300 
               3                0                0                0 

What gives?? Are the estimations regarding transitive term reliable? Do the simulations involving the transitive term yield reliable networks?

Dr. Kerimcan Ozcan

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] A question about ERGMs and simulating networks with an arbitrary number of nodes
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dave and the rest of the list,

Thanks for the response. Apologies if the question was confusing --  
what I was wondering about if it would be possible to:

* fit an ERGM model into a network dataset with n nodes
* create a model with the *same* ERGM model coefficients, but for m !=  
n nodes
* draw graph samples from that model.

Another way of saying this would be that given a graph with some  
attribute data, I would like to generate random graphs which are  
statistically similar to it (in terms of homophily, number of  
triangles, etc.) but which have a smaller (or larger) number of nodes  
than the original graph.

Is there an easy way to do this?

kind regards,

-- Hannu
